references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, Israel's service under Cushan-Rishathaim is described, which lasted eight years, establishing the pattern of oppression as a result of sin.
The context for Eglon's rule over Israel, where God strengthened Eglon against Israel because of their wickedness, and he allied himself with the Ammonites and Amalekites.
After eighteen years of oppression, the Israelites cried out to the Lord, and He raised up Ehud as a deliverer.
Moses' prophetic warning that Israel would serve their enemies if they abandoned the Lord, which was fulfilled during Eglon's rule.
A similar pattern where Israel was oppressed for twenty years under Jabin, king of Canaan, illustrating the repeated cycle in the book of Judges.
Israel was given into the hand of the Midianites for seven years, another example of oppression as punishment for sin.
Israel was given into the hand of the Philistines for forty years, the longest period of oppression in the book of Judges.
